page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ic5.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by the x86_64 architecture. The server is equipped with an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, providing 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. Cache configuration includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI, alongside AES cryptographic acceleration. Memory is provisioned at 16.0 GB total, yielding an unusually dense 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU (a 1:1 compute-to-memory ratio). The configuration includes no local storage and no dedicated hardware GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage while providing 5 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark results reflect the instance's 16-thread capacity contrasted against its legacy Skylake-era single-core throughput. In multi-threaded evaluation, the instance hits middle-tier performance, logging 11,785.54 in stress-ng multi-core tests, a Geekbench multi-core score of 6,191.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 12,997.09. Clang software compilation (10,481.0) and ray tracing (10,435.0) achieve solid median scores. Conversely, single-thread performance is constrained, demonstrated by a weak Geekbench single-core score of 991.0, a stress-ng single-core score of 1,105.99, and bottom-decile single-threaded gzip compression at 19.22 GB/sec. Memory subsystem evaluation shows 74.68 GB/sec read and 43.33 GB/sec write throughput for large blocks, alongside an overall PassMark memory score of 1,695.78.

Hardware tradeoffs center on its low memory-to-vCPU ratio. With only 1 GB of memory per core and no included local storage, large in-memory frameworks or data-intensive caching layers face strict resource ceilings. This is evidenced in LLM execution, where medium (7B) model inference achieves only 19.4 prompt tokens per second and 8.74 generation tokens per second, while 70B models cannot run due to memory limits. Cost efficiency is favored when running concurrent, parallelized compute tasks that fully saturate 16 threads without requiring large memory allocations. Primary suitable workloads include multi-threaded batch processing, distributed compilation, static web server fleets, and horizontal microservices that rely on network storage.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ic5.4xlarge is a compute-optimized x86_64 server running on KVM hypervisors. It features a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8163 processor configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs (8 physical cores across 16 threads) and 16.0 GB of system RAM, establishing an aggressive 1:1 compute-to-memory allocation. The instance includes no bundled local disks or GPUs, maintaining 5 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. Benchmarks establish dependable multi-core performance, recording 11,785.54 in stress-ng and 6,191.0 in Geekbench multi-core, offset by weak single-core metrics such as a 991.0 Geekbench single-core score. Because the platform delivers high vCPU density with limited per-core memory, it offers cost-efficient scaling for compute-bound applications that do not demand large RAM footprints. Optimal workloads encompass parallel software compilation, static web serving, containerized services, and multi-threaded CPU batch processing.
